S.FORM: tee=ku pu-a-iisua sua makai cəpəŋ miana.
S.PHON: teeku puaiisua sua makai ʦəpəŋ miana
S.FORM: teeku puaiisua sua makai cepeng miana.
S.PHON: teeku puaiisua sua makai ʦepeŋ miana
S.TRANSL: I will talk about what I can remember of in the past.
In the past, we were still working with each other.
We went to Tane'ece (to work) everyday.
At that time there were still many Kanakanavu people.

S.FORM: ʔaisi kaa-vaŋvaŋ na=cina ʔuusu na=cina piiʔi.
S.PHON: ʔaiʂi kaavaŋvaŋ natʂina ʔuusu natʂina piiʔi
ʔaiʂi kaavaŋvaŋ natʂina ʔuusu natʂina piiʔi
S.TRANSL: Michiko's mother 'Uusu and 'Uusu's mother Pii'i were all still living then.
At that time older women were still all around.

S.FORM: mia-iisua ia, sua miciko=maku mia-iisua, mia-iisua ia, ni-pu-aiʔi=cu ni-ara-anai ʔuma-ʔuma.
S.PHON: miaiisua ia sua mitʂikomaku miaiisua miaiisua ia nipuaiʔiʦu niaraanai ʔumaʔuma
S.FORM: miaiisua ia, sua micikomaku miaiisua, miaiisua ia, nipuai'icu niaraanai 'uma'uma.
S.PHON: miaiisua ia sua mitʂikomaku miaiisua miaiisua ia nipuaiʔiʦu nia[r|ɾ]aanai ʔumaʔuma
S.TRANSL: My wife Michiko returned from the fields at that time.
The other people returned home.

FORM.notes: Source parenthetical expanded under POL-026/POL-027; exact source and decision are in source_notation_audit.csv.

S.TRANSL: "Where is my wife Michiko?" I asked them.

FORM.notes: Source parenthetical expanded under POL-026/POL-027; exact source and decision are in source_notation_audit.csv.

S.TRANSL: "Where is my wife Michiko?" I asked them.

S.PHON: maɾivaɾi ʔikua ʦaau kan niivatuʦu misai
ma[r|ɾ]iva[r|ɾ]i ʔikua ʦaau kan niivatuʦu misai
S.TRANSL: The people replied to me, "She has already come (home)."
"She is not (home) yet," I said.

S.FORM: u-kusa-i ʔikua ni-ʔuna-ini tara-saŋai, ʔaisi ʔinia maka-naŋu-naŋulu ta-sikaar-a canumu.
S.PHON: ukusai ʔikua niʔunaini tarasaŋai ʔaiʂi ʔinia makanaŋunaŋuɾu taʂikaara ʦanumu
S.FORM: ukusai 'ikua ni'unaini tarasangai, 'aisi 'inia makanangunanguru tasikaara canumu.
S.PHON: ukusai ʔikua niʔunaini ta[r|ɾ]asaŋai ʔaiʂi ʔinia makanaŋunaŋu[r|ɾ]u taʂikaa[r|ɾ]a ʦanumu
S.TRANSL: I went to their rest area, (I found that) she was swimming in the water.

S.FORM: mia-iisua ia, ʔuuna apunuunaŋ mu-kusa ʔinia pita-sikarə cuu-canum.
S.PHON: miaiisua ia ʔuuna apunuunaŋ mukusa ʔinia pitaʂikarə ʦuuʦanum
S.FORM: miaiisua ia, 'uuna apunuunang mukusa 'inia pitasikare cuucanum.
S.PHON: miaiisua ia ʔuuna apunuunaŋ mukusa ʔinia pitaʂika[r|ɾ]e ʦuuʦanum
S.TRANSL: At that time, a ghost went there to draw her into water.
I went to her to lift her and called her, "Michiko!"
She replied to me, "What? What?"
It seemed to me that she did not recognize me.
I was worried about it.
I put away the firewood she was carrying on her back.
I led her by hand and brought her home.
I was to ask a priest-shaman to check her.
It seemed to me that she had been caught and had been played tricks on by a ghost.
My Michiko has stayed home ever since that happened.
She did not go to work following (the other people).
She was scared.

S.FORM: maka-sua sua si-a-tuuturu=maku kamua kin-va-vaal-a ŋuaci kari=maku.
S.PHON: makasua sua ʂiatuuturumaku kamua kinvavaaɾa ŋuatʂi karimaku
S.FORM: makasua sua siatuuturumaku kamua kinvavaara nguaci karimaku.
S.PHON: makasua sua ʂiatuutu[r|ɾ]umaku kamua kinvavaa[r|ɾ]a ŋuatʂi ka[r|ɾ]imaku
S.TRANSL: That's all I want to tell you, my siblings, with these words.
